instruction: Open the Slide Master view using View > Master > Slide Master, find the slide number placeholder, and apply red color formatting to it

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Paraphrased version of original task - same requirement (red color) but different wording. The evaluator uses the existing check_page_number_colors function which parses the slide master XML to verify the color of the page number placeholder.
metadata.verification: The check_page_number_colors function from slides.py (lines 876-920) parses the slide master XML to find the color of the page number placeholder. It checks the second-to-last solidFill/srgbClr element in the slide master and verifies it matches the expected color using threshold-based RGB comparison (red: R > G+50 and R > B+50, blue: B > G+50 and B > R+50, green: G > R+50 and G > B+50, black: R < 50 and G < 50 and B < 50).

llm_judge_reasons: The evaluator correctly uses check_page_number_colors to verify the page number placeholder color in the slide master
Function correctly handles expected parameter: directly accesses rules['color'] (not rules.get('rules', {})) which is correct for type='rule'
Appropriate threshold-based RGB color comparison (R > G+50 and R > B+50 for red) provides tolerance for color variations
Postconfig properly saves the file before evaluation using Ctrl+S
Complete coverage: checks the exact requirement (red color on page number placeholder)
Minor concern: Function relies on fragile heuristic (second-to-last solidFill/srgbClr element) which assumes specific XML structure - may not be robust across different presentation templates
Edge case handling could be improved: no explicit check for color_elems length before accessing [-2] index
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding explicit validation: check if len(color_elems) >= 2 before accessing color_elems[-2] to handle edge cases
